title: Lesson 7. Flexbox — practice, nested containers
description: flex-wrap, gap, nested flex, flex: 1 and a card gallery

learn.intro: Hi! Lesson 7 — Flexbox practice. There is almost no theory: we solve real tasks found on any site. Four tricks: `flex-wrap`, `gap`, nested containers and `flex: 1`. Let's go!

slides.text: Normally flex tries to fit all items in **one** row. If space is short, items shrink (`flex-shrink: 1`), and if shrinking is forbidden they overflow the container and a horizontal scroll appears.
The fix is one line on the container:
Like words in text: didn't fit — moved to the next line. The default is `nowrap`. And `flex-wrap` goes on the **parent**, not the children.

options: Moves items that don't fit to a new row

check.prompt: flex-wrap should be written on each card, not on the container.
check.explain: flex-wrap goes on the parent (the container).

slides.text: The old way — a margin on every card:
The problem: extra 20px to the right of the last card and under the last row. The new way is one line on the container, and the space goes only **between** items:
Two axes separately: `gap: 30px 10px;` — the first is between **rows**, the second between **columns** (the same as `row-gap` and `column-gap`).

check.prompt: Where does gap put the space?
check.explain: So there is no extra 20px at the edges.

check.prompt: Which property adds space only between rows?
check.explain: row-gap is between rows, column-gap between columns.

slides.text: One element can play two roles: for its parent it is a flex **item**, for its own children a flex **container**. Almost any interface is built like this, like a nesting doll.
A product card: image, name, description top to bottom, and at the bottom the price on the left and a button on the right in one row:
Each container controls only its **own** direct children. And `display: flex` is **not inherited** — write it on each container separately.

check.prompt: Is display: flex inherited by children?
options: No, it is written separately for each container
check.explain: This is a common beginner mistake.

check.prompt: One element can be a flex item for its parent and a flex container for its children.

slides.text: `flex: 1` tells children «take free space equally with your neighbors». You get columns of equal width without a single px or percent:
The number is a **share**: `flex: 1`, `flex: 1`, `flex: 2` give 4 shares, and the third column takes 2/4 — half the width. Add a fourth column and all become equal by themselves.

check.prompt: Columns with flex: 1, flex: 1, flex: 2. What share does the third take?
check.explain: There are 4 shares in total, the third has 2 of them.

slides.text: 6 cards, 3 per row, 20px between them. Why not `width: 33.33%`? Three 33% take almost the whole width plus two 20px `gap`s — there is not enough room and the third drops down. First subtract the gaps, then divide:
The formula for N per row: `width: calc((100% - (N - 1) × gap) / N)`. For a phone: `@media (max-width: 600px) { .product { width: 100%; } }`.

Homework — a «3 advantages» block: `.features` (flex, row, gap) and three `.feature` with `flex: 1`, each containing an icon, a heading and text top to bottom, centered. Bonus: on a narrow screen the columns stack.

check.prompt: Which width gives exactly 3 cards per row with gap: 20px?

questions.prompt: What is the default value of flex-wrap?
What happens if items don't fit and flex-shrink is 0?
options: They overflow, a horizontal scroll appears
questions.explain: Without wrap and shrink they go past the edge.

questions.prompt: gap also puts space at the container edges.

questions.explain: The first value is rows, the second columns.

questions.prompt: Why is gap better than margin for cards?
options: It leaves no extra space at the edges
questions.explain: No :last-child or negative margins are needed.

questions.prompt: How do you put the price on the left and the button on the right in one row?
options: A separate flex container with justify-content: space-between
questions.explain: The inner container is a row.

questions.prompt: Match the element and its direction
What does margin-top: auto do on .product-footer in a column?
options: Pushes it to the bottom of the card
questions.explain: So buttons in cards of different heights line up.

questions.prompt: What does flex: 1 give all columns?
options: Equal width without px and percent
questions.explain: Each takes an equal share of free space.

questions.prompt: What happens if you add a fourth column with flex: 1?
How many shares in total for columns flex: 1, flex: 1, flex: 2?
Why doesn't width: 33.33% work for 3 cards with a gap?
options: The gaps aren't counted, the third drops down
questions.explain: You need calc with the gap subtracted.
